title: [18/2/2024] Number of motor vehicles per 1,000 inhabitants
prompt: The table below shows the number of motor vehicles per 1,000 inhabitants in eight countries in 1990 and 2000. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make a comparison where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the number of motor vehicles per thousand people in eight different countries in 1990 and 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, most countries witnessed an increase in vehicle ownership during this period, with the exception of the Bahamas and Cambodia, where the figures fell and remained unchanged respectively. In addition, Brazil and Romania experienced extraordinary growth to become countries with the highest vehicle density by 2000.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at developed nations with high vehicle numbers, Luxembourg led the group with 548 vehicles per thousand inhabitants in 1990, slightly higher than New Zealand's 531, while the Bahamas recorded a considerably lower figure of 235. By 2000, Luxembourg's number had risen to 728, and New Zealand saw a modest increase to 557 vehicles. In contrast, the Bahamas experienced a decline to 187 vehicles per thousand people.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining countries, their initial figures in 1990 were significantly lower, with Cambodia recording just 1 vehicle per thousand people, while Jordan, Brazil, Chile and Romania had similar numbers ranging from 50 to 70 vehicles. Brazil showed the most dramatic change as its figure surged to 13,580 by 2000, followed by Romania with 8,012 vehicles. The other countries saw more modest increases, with Jordan's number rising to 157 vehicles and Chile's to 88, while Cambodia's figure remained unchanged.
